chunks: Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Shamun, from Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Misma' ibn Abd al-Malik, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) saw a man with dishevelled hair on his head, dirty clothes, and in a bad state. So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'From the Religion is the enjoyment and the manifestation of the Bounty.'

key_terms.إِظْهَارُ النِّعْمَةِ: The manifestation/display of Allah's blessings — showing gratitude by making one's receipt of God's favors visible through one's appearance and lifestyle
key_terms.الْمُتْعَةُ: In this context means 'enjoyment/beautification' — taking advantage of and beautifying oneself with Allah's blessings, not the separate jurisprudential term for temporary marriage
key_terms.شَعِثاً: Dishevelled, unkempt — describing hair that is matted and uncombed, a state of neglect
key_terms.وَسِخَةً: Dirty, soiled — describing clothes that are unclean and neglected

ai.seo_question: What does Islam say about personal grooming and appearance?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) narrates a teaching from the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW), who upon seeing a man in a state of visible neglect — unkempt hair, dirty clothes, and a poor overall appearance — declared that beautification and displaying Allah's blessings upon oneself are part of religion itself. This hadith teaches that Islam encourages its followers to take care of their appearance and outward presentation as an expression of gratitude for divine favors. The Arabic term 'al-mut'ah' here means taking pleasure in and beautifying oneself with Allah's bounties, not neglecting them, as an act of worship and thankfulness.
